questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Arrange the following compounds in the decreasing order of their acidic strength.
(I) m-cresol
(II) Phenol
(III) m-aminophenol
(IV) m-methoxyphenol
questions.solution:
At meta position, only inductive effect (I-effect) operates, not resonance.

m-methoxyphenol: $-OCH_3$ has strong $-I$ effect (O is highly electronegative) \to stabilizes phenoxide \to most acidic.

m-aminophenol: $-NH_2$ has $-I$ effect but weaker than $-OCH_3$ (N less electronegative than O) \to more acidic than phenol.

Phenol: reference compound, no substituent.

m-cresol: $-CH_3$ has $+I$ effect \to destabilizes phenoxide \to least acidic.

Decreasing order: IV $ \gt $ III $ \gt $ II $ \gt $ I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compound cannot be prepared by Williamson's synthesis?
questions.solution:
Williamson synthesis involves the reaction of an alkoxide ion with an alkyl halide via an $S_{N}2$ mechanism. Since $S_{N}2$ reactions are highly sensitive to steric hindrance, the alkyl halide used must be primary for the reaction to proceed efficiently. If a tertiary alkyl halide is used, elimination (E2) becomes the dominant pathway, leading to the formation of an alkene instead of an ether.

In the case of $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_3 \mathrm{COC}\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_3$ (di-tert-butyl ether), the synthesis would require the reaction of a tert-butoxide ion with a tert-butyl halide. Because the tert-butyl halide is a tertiary substrate, it undergoes rapid elimination to form isobutylene rather than substitution. Therefore, di-tert-butyl ether cannot be prepared by Williamson synthesis.

Answer: $\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_3 \mathrm{COC}\left(\mathrm{CH}_3\right)_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following tests may be used to distinguish between phenol and cyclohexanol?
questions.solution:
Phenol is an aromatic compound containing a hydroxyl group attached directly to a benzene ring, which imparts acidic character to the molecule. Cyclohexanol is an aliphatic cyclic alcohol.

The ferric chloride test is a characteristic test for phenols. Phenols react with neutral ferric chloride solution to form a violet, green, or blue colored complex, which is due to the formation of iron-phenolate complexes. Cyclohexanol, being an aliphatic alcohol, does not give this test.

The Hinsberg test is used to distinguish between primary, secondary, and tertiary amines. The iodoform test is used to detect the presence of a methyl ketone group or a methyl carbinol group (C$H_3$CH(OH)-). Reaction with sodium metal is given by both phenols and alcohols due to the presence of the hydroxyl group, so it cannot distinguish between them.

Answer: Ferric chloride test

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The major product '$\mathrm{X}$' of the following reaction is
questions.solution:
The reaction is an acid-catalyzed dehydration of a secondary alcohol, 3,3-dimethylpentan-2-ol. The mechanism proceeds via the formation of a carbocation intermediate.

Protonation of the hydroxyl group by $H_{2}SO_{4}$ to form a good leaving group, $-OH_{2}^{+}$.

Loss of water molecule to form a secondary carbocation at the C2 position: $CH_{3}-CH^{+}-C(CH_{3})_{2}-CH_{2}-CH_{3}$.

The secondary carbocation undergoes a 1,2-methyl shift to form a more stable tertiary carbocation: $CH_{3}-CH(CH_{3})-C^{+}(CH_{3})-CH_{2}-CH_{3}$.

Elimination of a proton from the adjacent carbon to form the most stable alkene (Zaitsev product). The tertiary carbocation can lose a proton from the C2 position to form 2,3-dimethylpent-2-ene, which is a highly substituted and stable alkene.

Therefore, the major product is 2,3-dimethylpent-2-ene.

Answer: 2, 3-dimethylpent-2-ene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds undergo Aldol condensation followed by dehydration to give 3-phenylprop-2-en-1-al?
questions.solution:
The target product is 3-phenylprop-2-en-1-al, which is cinnamaldehyde. Its structure is $C_{6}H_{5}-CH=CH-CHO$.

The structure contains a phenyl group attached to a three-carbon chain with an aldehyde functional group at the end. This indicates that the condensation occurs between an aromatic aldehyde (benzaldehyde) and an aliphatic aldehyde (ethanal).

The reaction is a Claisen-Schmidt condensation, a type of crossed aldol condensation. Benzaldehyde ($C_{6}H_{5}CHO$) acts as the electrophile because it lacks $\alpha$-hydrogens, and ethanal ($CH_{3}CHO$) acts as the nucleophile because it possesses $\alpha$-hydrogens.

The reaction proceeds as follows: $C_{6}H_{5}CHO + CH_{3}CHO \xrightarrow{OH^{-}} C_{6}H_{5}CH(OH)CH_{2}CHO \xrightarrow{-H_{2}O} C_{6}H_{5}CH=CHCHO$.

Therefore, the reactants are benzaldehyde and ethanal.

Answer: Benzaldehyde and Ethanal

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An organic compound with molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_3 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{N}$ on hydrolysis gives compound '$\mathrm{X}$' which on treatment with $\mathrm{Cl}_2 / \mathrm{P}$ gives compound '$\mathrm{Y}$'. Compound '$\mathrm{Y}$' on reaction with $\mathrm{NH}_3$ gives '$\mathrm{Z}$'. The compound '$\mathrm{Z}$' is :
questions.solution:
The molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_3 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{N}$ corresponds to propionitrile ($\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{CN}$).

Hydrolysis of propionitrile ($\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{CN} + 2\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{COOH} + \mathrm{NH}_3$) yields propanoic acid as compound '$\mathrm{X}$'.

Treatment of propanoic acid with $\mathrm{Cl}_2 / \mathrm{P}$ is the Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction, which results in $\alpha$-chlorination: $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}_2 \mathrm{COOH} + \mathrm{Cl}_2 \xrightarrow{\mathrm{P}} \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CHClCOOH}$ (2-chloropropanoic acid) as compound '$\mathrm{Y}$'.

Reaction of 2-chloropropanoic acid with $\mathrm{NH}_3$ involves nucleophilic substitution of the chlorine atom by the amino group: $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CHClCOOH} + 2\mathrm{NH}_3 \rightarrow \mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{NH}_2)\mathrm{COOH} + \mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{Cl}$.

The product '$\mathrm{Z}$' is 2-aminopropanoic acid (alanine).

Answer: 2-aminopropanoic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Arrange the following amines in the decreasing order of their solubilities in water.
questions.solution:
The solubility of amines in water depends on their ability to form hydrogen bonds with water molecules. Amines with lower molecular weight and fewer hydrophobic alkyl groups are generally more soluble.

Compound [I] is aniline ($C_6H_5NH_2$), which contains a large hydrophobic phenyl group. This large hydrocarbon part significantly reduces its solubility in water.

Compound [II] is ethylamine ($CH_3CH_2NH_2$), a primary amine with a small alkyl group. It can form effective hydrogen bonds with water and has a smaller hydrophobic part compared to [I] and [III].

Compound [III] is diethylamine ($(CH_3CH_2)_2NH$), a secondary amine. Although it can form hydrogen bonds, it has two ethyl groups, making it more hydrophobic than ethylamine [II].

Comparing the hydrophobic character: The phenyl group in [I] is the most hydrophobic, followed by the two ethyl groups in [III], and then the single ethyl group in [II].

Therefore, the decreasing order of solubility is ethylamine [II] > diethylamine [III] > aniline [I].

Answer: II > III > I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 4-methyl benzamide (A) on reaction with ethanolic solution of $\mathrm{KOH}$ and bromine gives another compound (B). The compound (B) on treatment with benzoyl chloride gives compound (C). Identify the correct structure of compound (C) from the following.
questions.solution:
The reaction of 4-methylbenzamide with $Br_{2}$ and ethanolic $KOH$ is the Hofmann bromamide degradation reaction. This reaction converts an amide ($R-CONH_{2}$) into a primary amine ($R-NH_{2}$) with one less carbon atom.

Starting with 4-methylbenzamide ($CH_{3}-C_{6}H_{4}-CONH_{2}$), the Hofmann bromamide degradation yields 4-methylaniline ($p$-toluidine), which is $CH_{3}-C_{6}H_{4}-NH_{2}$. This is compound (B).

Compound (B), 4-methylaniline, then reacts with benzoyl chloride ($C_{6}H_{5}-COCl$) in the presence of a base (like pyridine or aqueous $NaOH$) to form an amide through a nucleophilic acyl substitution reaction. This is the Schotten-Baumann reaction.

The reaction is: $CH_{3}-C_{6}H_{4}-NH_{2} + C_{6}H_{5}-COCl \rightarrow CH_{3}-C_{6}H_{4}-NH-CO-C_{6}H_{5} + HCl$.

The resulting product (C) is $N$-(4-methylphenyl)benzamide, which corresponds to the structure where the nitrogen atom is attached to the 4-methylphenyl group and the carbonyl group of the benzoyl moiety. This matches the first structure provided in the options.

Answer:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
With reference to vitamins and its deficiency diseases, the correct statements are:
(i) Cheilosis is due to the deficiency of Riboflavin
(ii) The deficiency of Vitamin B6 causes pernicious anaemia
(iii) Osteomalacia is due to the deficiency of Vitamin E
(iv) The deficiency of ascorbic acid causes scurvy
(v) The deficiency of Vitamin A causes xerophthalmia
questions.solution:
Statement (i) is correct: Riboflavin (Vitamin $B_2$) deficiency leads to cheilosis, which is the fissuring at the corners of the mouth and lips.

Statement (ii) is incorrect: Pernicious anaemia is caused by the deficiency of Vitamin $B_{12}$ (cyanocobalamin), not Vitamin $B_6$.

Statement (iii) is incorrect: Osteomalacia is caused by the deficiency of Vitamin D, not Vitamin E.

Statement (iv) is correct: Ascorbic acid is Vitamin C, and its deficiency leads to scurvy, characterized by bleeding gums and loose teeth.

Statement (v) is correct: Vitamin A deficiency leads to xerophthalmia, a condition characterized by the hardening of the cornea of the eye.

Therefore, the correct statements are (i), (iv), and (v).

Answer: $\text { (i), (iv) and (v) }$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statement is not true about glucose?
options: Glucose on reaction with $\mathrm{HI}$ and red $\mathrm{P}$ at $373 \mathrm{~K}$ gives a mixture of cyclohexane and 1-iodohexane
Glucose reacts with hydroxylamine to form an oxime
Glucose does not give Schiff's reagent test
Both $\alpha$-D-glucose and $\beta$-D-glucose undergo mutarotation in aqueous solutions
questions.solution:
Glucose is an aldohexose with the structure $CHO(CHOH)_{4}CH_{2}OH$.

Reaction with $HI$ and red phosphorus at $373 \text{ K}$ reduces glucose to $n$-hexane, not a mixture of cyclohexane and 1-iodohexane. This reaction confirms the presence of a straight chain of six carbon atoms in glucose.

Glucose reacts with hydroxylamine ($NH_{2}OH$) to form an oxime, confirming the presence of a carbonyl group.

Although glucose contains an aldehyde group, it does not give the Schiff's reagent test because the aldehyde group exists in a hemiacetal form in the cyclic structure, which is in equilibrium with a very small amount of the free aldehyde form in aqueous solution.

Both $\alpha$-D-glucose and $\beta$-D-glucose undergo mutarotation in aqueous solution, where they interconvert through the open-chain form until an equilibrium mixture is reached.

Answer: Glucose on reaction with $\mathrm{HI}$ and red $\mathrm{P}$ at $373 \mathrm{~K}$ gives a mixture of cyclohexane and 1-iodohexane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Among the following compounds, the most acidic is :
questions.solution:
The acidity of benzoic acid derivatives is determined by the electronic effects of the substituents present on the benzene ring.

The nitro group ($-NO_2$) is a strong electron-withdrawing group (EWG) due to both its negative inductive effect ($-I$) and negative resonance effect ($-M$). The methoxy group ($-OCH_3$) is an electron-donating group (EDG) due to its positive resonance effect ($+M$), which outweighs its negative inductive effect ($-I$) at the para position.

Comparing the given compounds:
1. 4-methoxybenzoic acid: The $-OCH_3$ group decreases the acidity of benzoic acid by donating electron density into the ring.
2. Benzoic acid: This is the reference compound.
3. 4-nitrobenzoic acid: The $-NO_2$ group increases the acidity of benzoic acid significantly due to its strong electron-withdrawing nature.
4. 3,4-dinitrobenzoic acid: This compound contains two $-NO_2$ groups. Both groups exert strong electron-withdrawing effects ($-I$ and $-M$). The presence of two such groups makes the carboxylate anion significantly more stable than in the case of 4-nitrobenzoic acid, thereby making 3,4-dinitrobenzoic acid the most acidic among the choices.

Answer: 3, 4-dinitrobenzoic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $\text { From the following pair of compounds, identify the incorrect pair in terms of the covalent character. }$
options: $A g C l\gt A g I$
questions.solution:
According to Fajan's rule, covalent character increases with smaller cation size, higher cation charge, and higher polarizability of the anion.

For option (KjFWQ), $\mathrm{Be}^{2+}$ is smaller than $\mathrm{Mg}^{2+}$, so $\mathrm{BeCl}_2$ has more covalent character than $\mathrm{MgCl}_2$. This is correct.

For option (U7Fpy), the cation $\mathrm{Ag}^{+}$ is the same. The anion $\mathrm{I}^{-}$ is larger and more polarizable than $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$. Therefore, $\mathrm{AgI}$ should have more covalent character than $\mathrm{AgCl}$. The statement $\mathrm{AgCl} \gt \mathrm{AgI}$ is incorrect.

For option (AHM95), $\mathrm{S}^{2-}$ is more polarizable than $\mathrm{O}^{2-}$ because sulfur is larger and less electronegative. Thus, $\mathrm{CuS}$ has more covalent character than $\mathrm{CuO}$. This is correct.

For option (xrYe2), $\mathrm{Sn}^{4+}$ has a higher charge than $\mathrm{Sn}^{2+}$, leading to greater polarization of the chloride ion. Thus, $\mathrm{SnCl}_4$ has more covalent character than $\mathrm{SnCl}_2$. This is correct.

Answer: $A g C l\gt A g I$

questions.q:
In the following question a statement of Assertion (A) followed by a statement of Reason (R) is given. Choose the correct option out of the choices given below.
Assertion (A): A molecule of $\mathrm{SF}_4$ is see-saw shaped, while that of $\mathrm{CIF}_3$ is T-shaped.
Reason(R): SF_4$ has two lone pair of electrons. But CIF_3$ has one pair of electrons.
options: Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is incorrect
Assertion (A) is incorrect but Reason (R) is correct
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are incorrect
questions.solution:
In $\mathrm{SF}_4$, the central sulfur atom has 6 valence electrons. It forms 4 bonds with fluorine atoms, leaving 2 electrons, which constitute 1 lone pair. The steric number is $4 + 1 = 5$, corresponding to a trigonal bipyramidal electron geometry. With one lone pair in the equatorial position, the molecular geometry is see-saw shaped. Thus, the assertion regarding $\mathrm{SF}_4$ is correct, but the reason stating it has two lone pairs is incorrect.

In $\mathrm{CIF}_3$, the central chlorine atom has 7 valence electrons. It forms 3 bonds with fluorine atoms, leaving 4 electrons, which constitute 2 lone pairs. The steric number is $3 + 2 = 5$, corresponding to a trigonal bipyramidal electron geometry. With two lone pairs in the equatorial positions, the molecular geometry is T-shaped. Thus, the assertion regarding $\mathrm{CIF}_3$ is correct, but the reason stating it has one lone pair is incorrect.

Since both statements in the Reason (R) are factually wrong, the Reason (R) is incorrect.

Answer: Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is incorrect

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: $\text{S}_8$ on heating at a temperature above 1000 K, changes to $\text{S}_2(g)$. When $\text{S}_8$ is heated above 1000 K at an initial pressure of 1 atm, the partial pressure of $\text{S}_8$ falls by 32% at equilibrium. The equilibrium constant for the conversion is:
questions.solution:
$S_8(g) \rightleftharpoons 4S_2(g)$

Initial pressure of $S_8 = 1$ atm. Pressure falls by 32%:
$P_{S_8} = 1 - 0.32 = 0.68$ atm
$P_{S_2} = 4 \times 0.32 = 1.28$ atm

$K_p = \dfrac{(P_{S_2})^4}{P_{S_8}} = \dfrac{(1.28)^4}{0.68} = \dfrac{2.684}{0.68} \approx 3.94$ atm$^3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The temperature $(\mathrm{T})$ and rate constant $(\mathrm{k})$ for a first order reaction $\mathrm{R} \rightarrow \mathrm{P}$, was found to follow the equation $\log \mathrm{k}=-(2000) \dfrac{1}{\mathrm{~T}}+8.0$. The pre-exponential factor '$\mathrm{A}$' and activation energy $\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{a}}$, respectively are: [Given: $\mathrm{R}=8.314 \mathrm{~J} \mathrm{~K}^{-1} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$]
questions.solution:
The Arrhenius equation is given by $k = A e^{-E_a / (RT)}$.

Taking the logarithm on both sides, we get $\log k = \log A - \dfrac{E_a}{2.303 RT}$.

Comparing this with the given equation $\log k = -2000 \left( \dfrac{1}{T} \right) + 8.0$, we identify the slope and the intercept.

The slope is $-\dfrac{E_a}{2.303 R} = -2000$.

Therefore, $E_a = 2000 \times 2.303 \times R = 2000 \times 2.303 \times 8.314 \text{ J mol}^{-1}$.

$E_a = 4606 \times 8.314 \approx 38294 \text{ J mol}^{-1} = 38.3 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

The intercept is $\log A = 8.0$.

Therefore, $A = 10^8 \text{ s}^{-1}$.

Answer: $1 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~s}^{-1} \text { and } 38.3 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The rate of appearance of bromine is related to the disappearance of bromide ion in the equation given below is:
$\mathrm{BrO}_3^{-} \text {(aq) }+5 \mathrm{Br}^{-} \text {(aq) }+6 \mathrm{H}^{+} \rightarrow 3 \mathrm{Br}_2(\mathrm{l})+3 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}(\mathrm{l})$
questions.solution:
For the given chemical reaction $\mathrm{BrO}_3^{-} + 5\mathrm{Br}^{-} + 6\mathrm{H}^{+} \rightarrow 3\mathrm{Br}_2 + 3\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$, the rate of reaction $r$ is expressed in terms of the rate of change of concentration of reactants and products as follows:

$r = -\dfrac{d[\mathrm{BrO}_3^{-}]}{dt} = -\dfrac{1}{5} \dfrac{d[\mathrm{Br}^{-}]}{dt} = -\dfrac{1}{6} \dfrac{d[\mathrm{H}^{+}]}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{3} \dfrac{d[\mathrm{Br}_2]}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{3} \dfrac{d[\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}]}{dt}$

We are interested in the relationship between the rate of appearance of bromine, $\dfrac{d[\mathrm{Br}_2]}{dt}$, and the rate of disappearance of bromide ion, $-\dfrac{d[\mathrm{Br}^{-}]}{dt}$.

From the rate expression, we have:

$-\dfrac{1}{5} \dfrac{d[\mathrm{Br}^{-}]}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{3} \dfrac{d[\mathrm{Br}_2]}{dt}$

Multiplying both sides by $3$, we get:

$\dfrac{d[\mathrm{Br}_2]}{dt} = -\dfrac{3}{5} \dfrac{d[\mathrm{Br}^{-}]}{dt}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}\left[\mathrm{Br}_2\right]}{\mathrm{dt}}=-\dfrac{3}{5} \dfrac{\mathrm{d}\left[\mathrm{Br}^{-}\right]}{\mathrm{dt}}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Given below a first order reaction in the gas phase
$\mathrm{A}(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow \mathrm{B}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{g})$
If the initial pressure of the system is $\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{i}}$ and the total pressure at $\mathrm{t}$ seconds is $\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{t}}$, the rate constant $\mathrm{k}$ for the reaction is:
questions.solution:
The reaction is $\mathrm{A}(\mathrm{g}) \rightarrow \mathrm{B}(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{C}(\mathrm{g})$.

At $t = 0$, the pressure of A is $P_i$, and the pressures of B and C are $0$.

At time $t$, let the decrease in pressure of A be $x$. Then the pressures of B and C are $x$ each. The pressure of A becomes $P_i - x$.

The total pressure $P_t$ at time $t$ is the sum of the partial pressures of all gases:

$P_t = (P_i - x) + x + x = P_i + x$

From this, $x = P_t - P_i$.

The partial pressure of A at time $t$ is $P_A = P_i - x = P_i - (P_t - P_i) = 2P_i - P_t$.

For a first-order reaction, the rate constant $k$ is given by:

$k = \dfrac{2.303}{t} \log \dfrac{P_i}{P_A}$

Substituting $P_A = 2P_i - P_t$, we get:

$k = \dfrac{2.303}{t} \log \dfrac{P_i}{2P_i - P_t}$

Answer: $\mathrm{k}=\dfrac{2.303}{\mathrm{t}} \log \dfrac{\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{i}}}{\left(2 \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{i}}-\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{t}}\right)}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: For the reaction, $\mathrm{A}+3 \mathrm{~B} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{C}+\mathrm{D}$, the concentration of $\mathrm{A}$ changes from 0.0150 to 0.0125 in 1 minute. The rate of formation of $\mathrm{C}$ in $\mathrm{mol} \mathrm{~L}^{-1} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$ is:
questions.solution:
The rate of reaction with respect to reactant A is given by the expression:

Rate $= -\dfrac{d[A]}{dt} = -\dfrac{[A]_2 - [A]_1}{t_2 - t_1}$

Given $[A]_1 = 0.0150 \text{ mol L}^{-1}$, $[A]_2 = 0.0125 \text{ mol L}^{-1}$, and $\Delta t = 1 \text{ minute} = 60 \text{ seconds}$.

Rate $= -\dfrac{0.0125 - 0.0150}{60} = \dfrac{0.0025}{60} = \dfrac{2.5 \times 10^{-3}}{60} \text{ mol L}^{-1} \text{ s}^{-1}$

From the stoichiometry of the reaction $\mathrm{A} + 3\mathrm{B} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{C} + \mathrm{D}$, the rate of reaction is also related to the rate of formation of C as:

Rate $= \dfrac{1}{2} \dfrac{d[C]}{dt}$

Therefore, $\dfrac{d[C]}{dt} = 2 \times \text{Rate} = 2 \times \dfrac{2.5 \times 10^{-3}}{60} = \dfrac{5.0 \times 10^{-3}}{60}$

$\dfrac{d[C]}{dt} = \dfrac{5}{6} \times 10^{-4} = 0.8333 \times 10^{-4} = 8.333 \times 10^{-5} \text{ mol L}^{-1} \text{ s}^{-1}$

Answer: $8.33 \times 10^{-5}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The half-life for a zero order reaction is
options: Directly proportional to the initial concentration and inversely proportional to the rate constant
Inversely proportional to the initial concentration and directly proportional to the rate constant
Independent of rate constant, but depends on the initial concentration
questions.solution:
For a zero order reaction, the integrated rate law is given by $[A] = [A]_0 - kt$, where $[A]_0$ is the initial concentration, $[A]$ is the concentration at time $t$, and $k$ is the rate constant.

The half-life $t_{1/2}$ is defined as the time when the concentration of the reactant is half of its initial value, i.e., $[A] = \dfrac{[A]_0}{2}$.

Substituting this into the rate equation:

$\dfrac{[A]_0}{2} = [A]_0 - kt_{1/2}$

$kt_{1/2} = [A]_0 - \dfrac{[A]_0}{2}$

$kt_{1/2} = \dfrac{[A]_0}{2}$

$t_{1/2} = \dfrac{[A]_0}{2k}$

From the expression $t_{1/2} = \dfrac{[A]_0}{2k}$, it is evident that the half-life is directly proportional to the initial concentration $[A]_0$ and inversely proportional to the rate constant $k$.

Answer: Directly proportional to the initial concentration and inversely proportional to the rate constant

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Among the following, which is not according to the property indicated against it?
options: $\mathrm{I}\lt \mathrm{Br}\lt \mathrm{F}\lt \mathrm{Cl} \text { [Increasing Elecrtron Gain Enthalpy with negative sign] }$
questions.solution:
Option (1): The electron gain enthalpy (magnitude) for halogens follows the order $\mathrm{I} \lt \mathrm{Br} \lt \mathrm{F} \lt \mathrm{Cl}$. Due to the small size of fluorine, interelectronic repulsions are high, making $\mathrm{Cl}$ have a more negative electron gain enthalpy than $\mathrm{F}$. This is correct.

Option (2): The first ionization enthalpy generally increases across a period. However, $\mathrm{N}$ has a stable half-filled $2p^3$ configuration, making its ionization enthalpy higher than that of $\mathrm{O}$. The correct order is $\mathrm{B} \lt \mathrm{C} \lt \mathrm{O} \lt \mathrm{N}$. Thus, the given statement is incorrect.

Option (3): For isoelectronic species, the ionic size increases as the nuclear charge decreases. The nuclear charges are $\mathrm{Mg}^{2+} (12)$, $\mathrm{Na}^{+} (11)$, $\mathrm{F}^{-} (9)$, and $\mathrm{O}^{2-} (8)$. The order $\mathrm{Mg}^{2+} \lt \mathrm{Na}^{+} \lt \mathrm{F}^{-} \lt \mathrm{O}^{2-}$ is correct.

Option (4): Metallic radii increase down a group due to the addition of new shells. The order $\mathrm{Na} \lt \mathrm{K} \lt \mathrm{Rb} \lt \mathrm{Cs}$ is correct.

Answer: $\mathrm{B}\lt \mathrm{C}\lt \mathrm{N}\lt \mathrm{O} \text { [Increasing First Ionisation Enthalpy] }$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The type of hybridisation and the spin only magnetic moment for the complex $[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO})_4]$ are respectively:
questions.solution:
The central metal atom is Nickel (Ni) with atomic number 28. The electronic configuration of Ni is $[Ar] 3d^{8} 4s^{2}$.

In the complex $[Ni(CO)_{4}]$, the oxidation state of Ni is 0, as CO is a neutral ligand. The configuration remains $[Ar] 3d^{8} 4s^{2}$.

CO is a strong field ligand, which causes the pairing of electrons in the $3d$ orbital. The two electrons from the $4s$ orbital are promoted to the $3d$ orbital to complete the $3d^{10}$ configuration, leaving the $4s$ and $4p$ orbitals vacant.

The four CO ligands donate electron pairs into one $4s$ and three $4p$ orbitals, resulting in $sp^{3}$ hybridization. This leads to a tetrahedral geometry.

Since all electrons are paired in the $3d^{10}$ configuration, the number of unpaired electrons $n = 0$. The spin only magnetic moment $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} = \sqrt{0(0+2)} = 0 \text{ BM}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{sp}^3$, zero

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The molar conductivity of the complex $\mathrm{CoCl}_3 \cdot 4 \mathrm{NH}_3 \cdot 2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ is found to be the same as that of a $1: 3$ electrolyte. The structural formula of the compound is :
questions.solution:
The molar conductivity of a $1:3$ electrolyte indicates that the complex dissociates into $4$ ions in total, consisting of one complex cation and three chloride anions. This implies that all three chloride ions are present outside the coordination sphere as counter ions.

The coordination number of Cobalt in such complexes is typically $6$. The formula given is $\mathrm{CoCl}_3 \cdot 4 \mathrm{NH}_3 \cdot 2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$.

If the complex is a $1:3$ electrolyte, the structure must be of the form $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O})_2]\mathrm{Cl}_3$. In this structure, the coordination sphere contains $4$ ammonia molecules and $2$ water molecules, satisfying the coordination number of $6$. The three chloride ions are outside the coordination sphere, which leads to the dissociation: $[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O})_2]\mathrm{Cl}_3 \rightarrow [\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}_3)_4(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O})_2]^{3+} + 3\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$.

This confirms the complex is a $1:3$ electrolyte.

Answer: $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_4\left(\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}\right)_2\right] \mathrm{Cl}_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: On the basis of crystal field theory, electronic configuration of a low spin $\mathrm{d}^4$ complex is:
questions.solution:
In an octahedral crystal field, the d-orbitals split into two sets: the lower energy $t_{2g}$ set and the higher energy $e_g$ set.

For a $d^4$ metal ion in a low spin complex, the crystal field splitting energy $\Delta_o$ is greater than the pairing energy $P$.

According to the Aufbau principle and Hund's rule, electrons fill the lower energy $t_{2g}$ orbitals first. Since the complex is low spin, pairing occurs in the $t_{2g}$ orbitals before any electrons occupy the $e_g$ orbitals.

For a $d^4$ configuration, the first three electrons occupy the $t_{2g}$ orbitals singly. The fourth electron pairs up in one of the $t_{2g}$ orbitals because $\Delta_o \gt P$.

Therefore, the electronic configuration is $t_{2g}^4 e_g^0$.

Answer: $t_{2 g}^4 e_g$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The metallic ions that have almost same spin only magnetic moment are :
(i) $\mathrm{Co}^{2+}$
(ii) $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$
(iii) $\mathrm{Cr}^{2+}$
(iv) $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}$
questions.solution:
The spin-only magnetic moment is calculated using the formula $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)}$ B.M., where $n$ is the number of unpaired electrons.

For $\mathrm{Co}^{2+}$ ($Z=27$): The electronic configuration is $[Ar] 3d^7$. The number of unpaired electrons $n = 3$. Thus, $\mu = \sqrt{3(3+2)} = \sqrt{15} \approx 3.87$ B.M.

For $\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$ ($Z=25$): The electronic configuration is $[Ar] 3d^5$. The number of unpaired electrons $n = 5$. Thus, $\mu = \sqrt{5(5+2)} = \sqrt{35} \approx 5.92$ B.M.

For $\mathrm{Cr}^{2+}$ ($Z=24$): The electronic configuration is $[Ar] 3d^4$. The number of unpaired electrons $n = 4$. Thus, $\mu = \sqrt{4(4+2)} = \sqrt{24} \approx 4.90$ B.M.

For $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}$ ($Z=24$): The electronic configuration is $[Ar] 3d^3$. The number of unpaired electrons $n = 3$. Thus, $\mu = \sqrt{3(3+2)} = \sqrt{15} \approx 3.87$ B.M.

Comparing the calculated magnetic moments, $\mathrm{Co}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Cr}^{3+}$ both have $n=3$ unpaired electrons and consequently the same spin-only magnetic moment of $\sqrt{15}$ B.M.

Answer: $\text { (i) and (iv) }$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Consider the following statements in respect of lanthanides, which of the statements are incorrect?
(i) $\mathrm{La}(\mathrm{OH})_3$ is least basic among the hydroxides of lanthanides
(ii) The lanthanide ions $\mathrm{Yb}^{2+}, \mathrm{Lu}^{3+}$ and $\mathrm{Ce}^{4+}$ are diamagnetic in nature.
(iii) $\mathrm{Ce}^{4+}$ can act as an oxidising agent
(iv) $\operatorname{Ln}$ (III) compounds are generally colourless
(v) Ionic radii of $\mathrm{Ce}^{3+}$ is greater than $\mathrm{Yb}^{3+}$
questions.solution:
Statement (i) is incorrect because basicity of lanthanide hydroxides decreases as the ionic radius decreases from $\mathrm{La}^{3+}$ to $\mathrm{Lu}^{3+}$. Thus, $\mathrm{La}(\mathrm{OH})_3$ is the most basic, not the least basic.

Statement (ii) is correct. $\mathrm{Yb}^{2+}$ has a $4f^{14}$ configuration, $\mathrm{Lu}^{3+}$ has a $4f^{14}$ configuration, and $\mathrm{Ce}^{4+}$ has a $4f^{0}$ configuration. All these have no unpaired electrons and are diamagnetic.

Statement (iii) is correct. $\mathrm{Ce}^{4+}$ has a strong tendency to gain an electron to form $\mathrm{Ce}^{3+}$ ($4f^{1}$), making it a good oxidizing agent.

Statement (iv) is incorrect. $\mathrm{Ln}^{3+}$ ions with $f^n$ configurations (where $n$ is between 1 and 13) exhibit $f-f$ transitions, which result in characteristic colors. Only $\mathrm{La}^{3+}$ ($f^0$) and $\mathrm{Lu}^{3+}$ ($f^{14}$) are colorless.

Statement (v) is correct. Due to lanthanide contraction, the ionic radii of $\mathrm{Ln}^{3+}$ ions decrease from $\mathrm{Ce}^{3+}$ to $\mathrm{Lu}^{3+}$. Therefore, the radius of $\mathrm{Ce}^{3+}$ is greater than that of $\mathrm{Yb}^{3+}$.

The incorrect statements are (i) and (iv).

Answer: (i) and (iv)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The correct order of increasing melting point is
questions.solution:
The melting points of transition metals depend on the strength of metallic bonding, which is related to the number of unpaired electrons available for delocalization in the metallic lattice. The electronic configurations of the given elements are:

$\mathrm{Ti} (3d^{2} 4s^{2})$
$\mathrm{V} (3d^{3} 4s^{2})$
$\mathrm{Cr} (3d^{5} 4s^{1})$
$\mathrm{Mn} (3d^{5} 4s^{2})$

Generally, the melting point increases as the number of unpaired electrons increases, reaching a maximum at the middle of the series. However, $\mathrm{Mn}$ has a stable half-filled $d$-subshell ($3d^{5}$), which makes its electrons less available for metallic bonding compared to its neighbors. This leads to a significantly lower melting point for $\mathrm{Mn}$ compared to $\mathrm{Cr}$, $\mathrm{V}$, and $\mathrm{Ti}$.

The melting points of these elements are approximately:
$\mathrm{Mn} \approx 1246 \, \mathrm{K}$
$\mathrm{Ti} \approx 1941 \, \mathrm{K}$
$\mathrm{V} \approx 2183 \, \mathrm{K}$
$\mathrm{Cr} \approx 2180 \, \mathrm{K}$

Comparing these values, the order of increasing melting point is $\mathrm{Mn} \lt \mathrm{Ti} \lt \mathrm{V} \lt \mathrm{Cr}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{Mn}\lt \mathrm{Ti}\lt \mathrm{V}\lt \mathrm{Cr}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
$\mathrm{Cu}^{+}$ undergoes disproportionation, according to the equation,
$
2 \mathrm{Cu}^{+} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{Cu}^{2+}+\mathrm{Cu}
$
The $\mathrm{E}^{\circ}$ value for the reaction is:
$[\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{Cu}^{2+} / \mathrm{Cu}}^{\mathrm{o}}=0.34 \mathrm{~V} \text { and } \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{Cu}^{2+} / \mathrm{Cu}^{+}}^{\mathrm{O}}=0.15 \mathrm{~V}]$
questions.solution:
The given disproportionation reaction is $2 \mathrm{Cu}^{+} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu}^{2+} + \mathrm{Cu}$.

This reaction can be split into two half-reactions:
1) Oxidation: $\mathrm{Cu}^{+} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu}^{2+} + e^{-}$ (where $E^{\circ}_{ox} = -E^{\circ}_{\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}/\mathrm{Cu}^{+}} = -0.15 \text{ V}$)
2) Reduction: $\mathrm{Cu}^{+} + e^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu}$ (where $E^{\circ}_{red} = E^{\circ}_{\mathrm{Cu}^{+}/\mathrm{Cu}}$)

To find $E^{\circ}_{\mathrm{Cu}^{+}/\mathrm{Cu}}$, we use the Gibbs free energy relation $\Delta G^{\circ} = -nFE^{\circ}$.
For $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+} + 2e^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu}$, $\Delta G^{\circ}_{1} = -2 \times F \times 0.34 = -0.68F$.
For $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+} + e^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu}^{+}$, $\Delta G^{\circ}_{2} = -1 \times F \times 0.15 = -0.15F$.
Subtracting the second from the first gives $\mathrm{Cu}^{+} + e^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cu}$, with $\Delta G^{\circ}_{3} = \Delta G^{\circ}_{1} - \Delta G^{\circ}_{2} = -0.68F - (-0.15F) = -0.53F$.
Thus, $E^{\circ}_{\mathrm{Cu}^{+}/\mathrm{Cu}} = -\Delta G^{\circ}_{3} / (1 \times F) = 0.53 \text{ V}$.

The standard cell potential for the disproportionation reaction is $E^{\circ}_{cell} = E^{\circ}_{ox} + E^{\circ}_{red} = -0.15 \text{ V} + 0.53 \text{ V} = +0.38 \text{ V}$.

Answer: $+0.38$ V

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The limiting molar conductivity of $\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH}$ is $238 \mathrm{~S} \mathrm{~cm}^2 \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$. At $25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, molar conductance of $0.1 \mathrm{M}$ aqueous solution of ammonium hydroxide is $9.54 \mathrm{~S} \mathrm{~cm}^2 \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$. The degree of ionisation of $\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH}$ at the same concentration and temperature is:
questions.solution:
The degree of ionisation $\alpha$ of a weak electrolyte is given by the ratio of the molar conductivity at a given concentration $\Lambda_m^c$ to the limiting molar conductivity $\Lambda_m^{\circ}$.

$\alpha = \dfrac{\Lambda_m^c}{\Lambda_m^{\circ}}$

Given values are $\Lambda_m^c = 9.54 \text{ S cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$ and $\Lambda_m^{\circ} = 238 \text{ S cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$.

Substituting these values into the formula:

$\alpha = \dfrac{9.54}{238} \approx 0.040084$

To express this as a percentage, multiply by 100:

$\alpha \% = 0.040084 \times 100 = 4.0084 \%$

Answer: 4.008%

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The $\mathrm{E}^{\circ}$ values of $\mathrm{A} . \mathrm{B}$ and $\mathrm{C}$ are given. Which element/(s) is/(are) good for coating the surface of iron to prevent corrosion?
Given: $[\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{Fe}^{2+} / \mathrm{Fe}}^0=-0.44 \mathrm{~V} ; \quad \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{A}^{2+} / \mathrm{A}}^0=-2.37 \mathrm{~V} ; \quad \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{B}^{2+} / \mathrm{B}}^0=-0.15 \mathrm{~V} ; \quad \mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{C}^{2+} / \mathrm{C}}^0=+0.34 \mathrm{~V}]$
questions.solution:
To prevent the corrosion of iron, the metal used for coating must act as a sacrificial anode. This means the coating metal must have a more negative standard reduction potential than that of iron ($E^{\circ}_{Fe^{2+}/Fe} = -0.44 \text{ V}$).

Comparing the given standard reduction potentials:
$E^{\circ}_{A^{2+}/A} = -2.37 \text{ V}$
$E^{\circ}_{B^{2+}/B} = -0.15 \text{ V}$
$E^{\circ}_{C^{2+}/C} = +0.34 \text{ V}$

Since $-2.37 \text{ V} \lt -0.44 \text{ V}$, element A has a lower reduction potential than iron. Therefore, element A can act as a sacrificial anode and protect iron from corrosion.

Elements B and C have reduction potentials greater than $-0.44 \text{ V}$, meaning they are more noble than iron and would not provide sacrificial protection.

Answer: Element A only

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the incorrect statement among the following.
options: Electrolytic conductance increases with increase in temperature
Conductivity does not depend on the viscosity of the solution
Conductivity depends on the size of the ions
Conductivity depends on the solvation of the ions
questions.solution:
(1) Correct: With increase in temperature, kinetic energy of ions increases and viscosity of solvent decreases \to ions move faster \to conductance increases.

(3) Correct: Larger ions move more slowly \to lower mobility \to lower conductivity.

(4) Correct: Greater solvation \to larger effective ionic radius \to lower mobility \to lower conductivity.

(2) Incorrect: Ion mobility is inversely proportional to viscosity of the solution. Higher viscosity \to greater resistance to ion movement \to lower conductivity. So conductivity does depend on viscosity.

Incorrect statement: (2)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When 0.1 mole of $\mathrm{MnO}_4{ }^{2-}$ is oxidised, the quantity of electricity required to completely oxidise $\mathrm{MnO}_4{ }^{2-}$ to $\mathrm{MnO}_4^{-}$ is
questions.solution:
The oxidation reaction of manganate ion to permanganate ion is given by:

$\mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{2-} \rightarrow \mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{-} + e^{-}$

In this reaction, the oxidation state of manganese changes from $+6$ to $+7$. Thus, $1$ mole of $\mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{2-}$ requires $1$ mole of electrons for complete oxidation to $\mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{-}$.

Given that $0.1$ mole of $\mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{2-}$ is to be oxidized, the number of moles of electrons required is $0.1$ mole.

The quantity of electricity $Q$ is given by $Q = n \times F$, where $n$ is the number of moles of electrons and $F$ is the Faraday constant ($96500 \text{ C mol}^{-1}$).

$Q = 0.1 \text{ mol} \times 96500 \text{ C mol}^{-1} = 9650 \text{ C}$.

Answer: 9650 C

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Names of some organic compounds are given. Which one is not in IUPAC system?
questions.solution:
We evaluate the IUPAC names provided for each structure:

1. 1,3,3-trimethylcyclohex-1-ene: The numbering starts from the double bond. If we number the double bond as 1 and 2, the methyl groups are at positions 1 and 3,3. This is correct.

The substituents are 2,3-dimethyl and 4-oxo. The name should be 2,3-dimethyl-4-oxopent-2-enoic acid.
